clauses.reason: Paragraph 1 closes the departments and excuses employees from duty on one stated day: the text says the offices "shall be closed all day on" on "Tuesday, December 24,1940". The command is performed and spent on that day, December 24, 1940.

Paragraph 2 directs that the order "shall be published in the" Federal Register. The held text is the Federal Register issue headed "Washington, Wednesday, December 18, 1940", and the order's filing line reads December 17, 1940; the direction was performed by publication in the December 18, 1940 issue (5 FR 5143) and is spent then.

research_rationale:
EO 8613 is the order excusing Federal employees from duty on December 24, 1940. The held text is the official Federal Register issue of December 18, 1940 (5 FR 5143), as a machine text layer of the govinfo PDF; the order appears under its title with the trailing number line and the signature date December 16, 1940. The held text has two numbered paragraphs, so the inventory is two clauses: the closure and excusal for the stated day, and the direction to publish. Both are one-time commands performed on stated days: the closure on December 24, 1940 and publication in the issue dated December 18, 1940. The machine searches for the U.S. Code, eCFR and OFR catalog record no hit that affects the order. The text layer is OCR; quotations below are limited to single lines and were checked against the held bytes.

savings.reason: The excusal from duty was for one day only, December 24, 1940; once that day passed the excusal had been given and nothing in the text carries over. The excusal already given is the only accrued effect.
